utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'd like to start today with delivering a decision. It is a decision on the Cermak Defence request for leave to call two witnesses in response to the re-opened Prosecution's case. On the 19th of May, 2010, the Cermak Defence requested leave to call evidence in response to the re-opened Prosecution case and leave to call two proposed witnesses and to add them to its Rule 65 ter witness list. On the 20th of May, pursuant to Rule 126 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Chamber set the deadline for responding to the request at the 26th of May, 2010, and informed the parties accordingly by means of an informal communication. On the 26th of May, 2010, the Prosecution and the Gotovina Defence responded that they did not object to the request. On the 27th of May, the Chamber informed the parties that it granted the Cermak Defence's request and instructed the Cermak Defence to file an addendum to its Rule 65 ter witness list by the 1st of June. On the same day, the Markac Defence filed a late response, indicating that it, too, did not object to the request. The Chamber has not considered the Markac Defence's late response in reaching its decision. Under Article 21(4)(e) of the Statute of the Tribunal, the accused is entitled to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him. Pursuant to Rule 85(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Defence is entitled to present evidence after the Prosecution's evidence, unless otherwise directed by the Chamber. The Chamber considers that the other parties have not objected to the Cermak Defence request to call evidence in response to the Prosecution's re-opened case. The Chamber further considers that the expected testimony of the witnesses the Cermak Defence seeks to call in response relates directly to that of the witnesses called by the Prosecution in its re-opened case and that the time required for hearing the proposed witnesses would be limited. For these reasons, the Chamber grants the Cermak Defence's requests. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. For the next item, I'd like to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Cermak Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that your next witness is Mr. Vrticevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With the Court's leave, I call Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vrticevic. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, of which the text will now be handed out to you by Mr. Usher. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vrticevic. Please be seated. Mr. Vrticevic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Kay. Mr. Kay is counsel for Mr. Cermak. Mr. Kay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the screen in front of you, and I'm going to call up a document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And the document that should be coming will be a witness statement taken from you in your own language. If you could just look at that page there. And do you recognise as that being a witness statement that was taken from you and signed by you on the 13th of May, 2010?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'd like you now to look at the last page of that statement in your own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have two versions of the English language. If we could have the one in the witness's own language, please. That's the most important document here. We did have both versions of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you see there at the -- at the end of the statement taken from you, do you recognise there your signature, Mr. Vrticevic? We -- we seem to have gremlins in the system and it changes just as I'm referring to a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we just keep it on the last page, please. I promise I will be quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise there your signature, Mr. Vrticevic, at the end of this statement taken on the 13th of May, 2010?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And since that statement was taken from you and you signed it, have you had an opportunity to read through that statement carefully to check it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And is everything that is contained in that statement, to the best of your knowledge and belief, true and correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I was to ask you today in court the same questions, would you give the same answers and information as contained in that statement, if I asked those questions today?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In those circumstances, Your Honour, I request that this be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections from any party. Madam Registrar, the number of the 92 ter statement of Mr. Vrticevic would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D2052, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D2052 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions now about some other interviews that took place with you, Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, could we have Exhibit P2731 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. We had received no notification that that issue would be addressed. In the motion that General Cermak's counsel filed that Your Honour referred to today, the issue for which this witness was called was to rebut the previous evidence and to show the whereabouts of certain people. Similarly there's nothing in this 92 ter statement discussing any prior interviews. In addition, the exhibits that we received for this witness, until yesterday, only included the ones that were appended to the statement. Only at 9.06 this morning did we receive any notice that these interviews would be covered in the examination of this witness. And it's just not proper. It's too late. And therefore I would object to this whole line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I could do it without referring to the exhibit, if that inconveniences anyone to look at the paper. I don't mind doing that. I can do it by general questions. I was just seeking to assist the Court on matters that have arisen last week in this court and to ask this witness for his evidence on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, is it your position that you say I would as easily do without and just draw the attention of the Court to that statement, or do you -- or would you prefer and therefore ask the Chamber to rule on the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't require a ruling on it. I can deal with it just as simply without. I was attempting to assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: -- anyone who needed to be assisted; if they don't, then I won't do anything more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hedaraly, you'll understand that since we can manage ourselves, the e-court system, it may that be P2731 will be on the Judges' screens anyhow, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that apparently is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Maybe my objection was misunderstood. It was not to refer to the document, it was to that line of questioning for which we had received no notice. So if Mr. Kay puts questions to the witness, whether or not he relies on the exhibit itself, I agree with Mr. Kay and I agree with the Chamber that putting the document on the screen is not the issue. The issue is notice about a topic that was going to be addressed, and that's a notice that was not provided until 9.06 this morning and until Mr. Kay asked his first question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let me just see. The line of questioning -- the only thing we've heard, until now, is that Mr. Kay would ask some questions about some other interviews and asked P2731 to be on the screen. What the questions will be and in what way they are fit into the 65 ter summary, I do not know; and I think we have not received, not at six minutes past 9.00 this morning, any further notice. But perhaps I should check my e-mail and see whether it. I suggest that Mr. Kay continues his examination. And if there's any matter you think is -- is not in sufficiently direct relation to what is in the 65 ter summary, then we hear from you. Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, do you know Jozo Bilobrk?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you work with him in the Split-Dalmatia Police Administration Forensic Unit?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you ever interviewed by the Defence team for General Markac with Jozo Bilobrk?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were interviewed by police officers in the Republic of Croatia last year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to those interviews, did you withhold any information from the people interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to events at Grubori on the 27th of August, 1995, you were part of the forensic examination team that attended that village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On that day, did anyone ever suggest to you that weapons should be planted at the crime scene so that it looked like a combat action had taken place?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Bilobrk ever pass on information to you that a suggestion had been heard by him that that could happen?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, those are all the questions that I ask of the witness, and I provide him for the parties for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, will it be you or will it be Mr. Carrier who will cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think for Defence witnesses the other Defence teams first have an opportunity. I believe, if I remember correctly the procedure, Your Honour. I don't know if they have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see from the body language of Mr. Kehoe that he has no questions. Mr. Mikulicic -- Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, just one, possibly two, depending on the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, you have an opportunity to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Vrticevic, you are now cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Kuzmanovic is counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kay asked you a question about whether or not you were interviewed together with Mr. Bilobrk by any members of the Markac Defence, and your answer to that question was no. My question to you is: At any time in the last two years did you meet with or be interviewed by any member of the Markac Defence team?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Perhaps before -- one question, rather, to complete that matter. Have you ever been in any way in communication with the Markac Defence? Did you receive a phone call, did you write a letter, did they write you a letter, did -- was there any e-mail exchange? So was there ever any contact with the Simatovic Defence -- the -- I'm sorry. With the Markac Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hedaraly, you're ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Hedaraly, and Mr. Hedaraly is counsel for -- is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vrticevic.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you regarding the statement that you gave to the Cermak Defence team. First of all, you stated in that statement that looking at contemporaneous documents that you were shown you remember that you first went to Strmica on the 27th of August and then went to Plavno; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us whether this is something that you actually remember, as you sit here today, that you went to Strmica and that you then went to Plavno, or is it simply a conclusion that are you drawing from looking at these documents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You also stated that, on the morning of the 27th of August, before setting out that day to carry out your tasks, you were in a coffee-shop with some colleagues while Mr. Bilobrk went to the Knin Police Station to get reports; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You don't know what happened while Mr. Bilobrk went to the police station; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You don't know who he talked to or what specific instructions he may have received or anything of that sort, right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: According to your account, you went to Strmica first and then to Plavno. Do you remember stopping by the Knin cemetery to leave the corpse you had collected from Strmica on the way back?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you remember stopping at the cemetery on the way back?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And were you with the members of the civil protection the whole time while they were actually burying the corpse?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: At -- on certain occasions we would be with them, on others we wouldn't. And I can't recall specifically on that day whether we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: When you say "we" in that answer, you mean you and Mr. Bilobrk?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you don't know if, on that day, when you came back to the -- when the -- when your colleagues from civil protection buried the body in the cemetery, whether you were there or whether you were maybe in town in Knin having a coffee or something else, right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if I was present while they were burying them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness come closer to the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, could you please come a bit closer to the microphone because the interpreters have difficulties hearing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On your way to Grubori --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just looking at that question, he never mentioning anything about having a coffee at the time, and maybe it should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it should be explored in a bit more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On the days when you would not stay at the -- let me start again. You said sometimes you would stay at the cemetery while the bodies would be buried and sometimes you would not. On the days where would you not, if you remember, what did you do, generally?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On your way to Grubori, you were stopped in the village of Plavno; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You don't know why you were stopped; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You don't know whether the group that was assembled there was waiting for you and your colleagues and wanted to discuss a matter with you; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You already knew who Mr. Cermak was when you arrived at that -- in Plavno; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I had previously only seen him on TV, and that was the first time I saw him in real life, so to speak, and I didn't know what his function was.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, could you invite the witness to repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer. I'm not sure we received the complete interpretation of your answer. If could you repeat last portion, please.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: So I had previously seen Mr. Cermak on TV. That was the first time I saw him. But I didn't know what his function was or what he was charged with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. My question was simply if you already knew who he was, not about his functions. But I understand your answer. Now, at that -- at that that location in Plavno, there was a discussion and there was some argument; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There was no argument about whether journalists should film you while you carried out your tasks?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: That's a different matter. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, it's not a different matter. I asked you whether there was a discussion and some argument, and you said no. I mean, I don't think I understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So there was an argument there?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you reacted unfavourably to the suggestion that journalists film you while you carried out your tasks; right?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't agree to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You didn't -- did you not want anyone filming you while you were collecting bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember who made the suggestion that journalists should film you and your colleagues on that day?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Was there also an argument regarding whether or not to carry [sic] an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember even generally any discussion about an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter 7622. And that is the statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in March earlier this year. Do you remember that interview that you had with the Office of the Prosecutor on the 4th of March, 2010?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is your signature at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in the course of that interview, you were shown various interview notes that had been prepared by colleagues of yours from the police force; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to paragraph 3, the second page of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you say there: "I also reviewed the Official Note of the second interview with Robert Badzim of the MUP (first page stamped with number 0673-8523). This note is generally accurate, but I am willing to repeat the whole story again." Let me now show you that note that you referred to as generally accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that is P2734.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you'll see the number on the top is the same one referred -- that was in your statement. And at the bottom, in the English, the last sentence reads: "General Cermak asked Vrticevic to do an on-site investigation in the village of Grubori, but he replied that in order to do an on-site investigation he needed to notify the State Prosecutor, an investigative judge, and a forensic officer to assist the investigative judge." The end will appear in the English on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You have to turn the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, in your OTP statement you said that this note was generally accurate. So can you explain whether or not there was any discussion of an on-site investigation on that day?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: This note drafted by the gentleman who held the interview is quite inaccurate. And you will recall, sir, when you interviewed me, that I told you at the outset that we would not be looking at this as much, that it was quite superficial, that it wasn't properly drafted, and that I would be giving you the details concerning this event, if you remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What is in your statement and what I remember and it's clear in your statement you were shown three different interview notes. And that one is the only one that you agreed was generally accurate when you reviewed them. So what I'm telling you is, are you now saying that this note isn't accurate when you said on 4 March 2010 that this -- this one specifically, not the other ones, was generally accurate?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall whether I said that it was accurate or inaccurate. But let me repeat. I said that I would recount the events of the day again, and you agreed with me, that this is what we would do during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you want to look back at the statement and see what you said? Because you also signed that interview after it was read back to you, correct, and you confirmed that it was accurate? I mean, we can look back if you want, the portion I read you about that note being -- being generally accurate. That's all I'm focussing on now, not on what else happened in the interview but whether you stated that this note on the screen was generally accurate.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: You read the statement back to me, and I signed it; but I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's right. But when it was read back to you, it was accurate, in terms of what you heard, and then you signed it; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: It's hard to remember everything. The entire statement was read back to me, and it was read back. It's difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me move on. Let me then go back to the OTP statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And go to the rest of your statement where you were actually telling the story as had you -- as you had expressed a desire to do. And this time I want to go to paragraph 9 when it comes up on the screen. And in paragraph 9, you then stated: "During the first interview with Badzim" -- and that's the joint one, not the one we just saw but the one with you and Mr. Bilobrk together, "... I remember Bilobrk stating that someone had requested an on-site investigation and some argument regarding this. When I heard this, it rang a bell, but I really can't remember any details." Was that the truth, that you heard some general comment about an on-site investigation and that when -- sorry. Is it true that when Mr. Bilobrk mentioned that at the joint interview, it did ring a bell but you couldn't remember the details?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I heard Bilobrk mention this, as is written here, but I really don't remember that. That's why I told you so, that I didn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well you said it rang a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, the statement says that it rang a bell, but you didn't remember the details. Now when you gave that statement, did you say that you didn't remember the details but that, when hearing Bilobrk stating about this conversation on an on-site investigation, did you tell the Prosecutor that it did ring a bell but that you didn't remember the details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If that's what is written here, then I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to hear from you whether that's what you said or not. Was that, in your recollection, what was read back to you; and is that what you signed for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's hard to remember, Your Honour. Who could remember that? I was recounting the whole story five or six times already. It's difficult to keep track of everything. I know that when we met at that particular cross-roads in Plavno, that I wasn't close by. I was having a smoke with the colleagues from the civilian protection, Jozo was there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking about what happened at the time. I'm asking you whether, when you were interviewed by the Office of the Prosecution, whether you stated that hearing Bilobrk talking about or stating about a conversation on an on-site investigation, that you, at that moment - that is, March of this year - whether you said, Well, it does ring a bell but that I don't remember the details. Is that what you said or is it -- or didn't you say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember anymore. I can't give you a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: As you sit here today, does the mention of an on-site investigation ring a bell at all as one of the possible topics of conversations you may have heard or been involved in?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: When you arrived in Grubori, did you conduct an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In all the cases where you carried [sic] sanitation operations after Operation Storm, did you ever conduct any on-site investigations?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you ever refuse to answer any questions because it would be detrimental to the generals?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In the joint interview that you had with Mr. Bilobrk, did Bilobrk -- did Mr. Bilobrk mention having been interviewed by members of the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that he had been with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: He also said that to the person that was interviewing both of you together; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in that interview, although I understand you didn't say it, did Mr. Bilobrk refuse to answer questions that would be detrimental to the generals?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, we can look at it. That joint interview states that those comments were made by you and him, and I understand it was a joint interview, and one of the concerns you had was that it's not clear who had said what. I can show it to you, if you want. But my simple question is: You said you didn't say such a thing. In that interview, do you remember Mr. Bilobrk saying he would not answer questions because they would be detrimental to the generals?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. The only thing I know is that Mr. Bilobrk told that colleague that he had been interviewed by the Defence for General Markac a while before that particular interview took place. That's something I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In that joint interview, do you remember who was answering most of the questions that were -- that were put to both of you? Was it both of you answering together, was it mainly Mr. Bilobrk, or was it mainly you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Those are my questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, I have a few questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, you said that you had seen Mr. Cermak on TV. Let me read what was -- what we find on our transcript. You were asked: "You already knew who Mr. Cermak was when you arrived at that -- in Plavno; correct?" Your answer was: "I had previously only seen him on TV, and that was the first time I saw him in real life, so to speak, and I didn't know what his function was." And then you were invited to repeat the last part of your answer. And you said: "So I" -- and there the text is a bit unclear. I take it that it should read: "So I had previously seen Mr. Cermak on TV. That was the first time I saw him. But I didn't know what his function was or what he was charged with." Could you tell us, in what context did you see him on television before the day you went to Grubori?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I saw him a number of times on TV, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell me in what context? What was it about that he was telling you on television?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you also said that you didn't know what he was charged with. Why did you mention this, that, apparently, you didn't know when you saw him what he was charged with?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: That was how I understood the Prosecutor's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you went on that day first to Strmica. Do you -- could you tell us any further details on that day? At what time in the morning did you receive instructions to go to Strmica, or where were you when you were informed about going to Strmica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly where I was, but my colleague Bilobrk always went to the station, and he received orders about where we should go and what we needed to do. I don't remember whether I was in a cafe or in a car or at the cemetery. Sometimes there was no work in the morning, so we wouldn't be at the cemetery because there was no need for the sanitation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Do you remember at what time approximately you heard that you would be heading for Strmica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection on what you found in Strmica? Was it the ordinary thing; one body, more bodies? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember how much time it took you to -- to go from Knin to Strmica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember how much time you spent on doing the job in Strmica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember how much time it took you to get back to Knin? But, first, you did go back to Knin first; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, could you tell us, what did you do in Knin? Did you and Mr. Bilobrk, or you alone, or Mr. Bilobrk alone, go to the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: We always went together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On that day, did you go to the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We always went there together, let me repeat that, Your Honour. We never separated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You mean you did not separate from Mr. Bilobrk, or did you not separate from the -- the people who accompanied you? Perhaps you tell us exactly what the team was you went to Strmica with. It was you, Mr. Bilobrk, and who else?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Most probably civil protection. I cannot remember the names from the people from the civilian protection who were working with us on a daily basis in the same team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many of them were with you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: They went in a van. There were two people, at least. Never less than two. Two men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did they transport the body that was found in Strmica to the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you accompany them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: We did reach the cemetery, but whether we waited for the burial or not, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who would be in charge of the burial?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Also our colleagues from civilian protection who were working with the excavator and who placed crosses and who also had to determine whether the identity of the person had been established or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be the same persons you were with that accompanied you to and from Strmica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: They were a team, but sometimes they would switch. Some had to go into the field and some remained at the cemetery, so I cannot remember who it was because they switched places sometimes. But these were the people who were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On that day, did the team you were with, the civilian protection team, did that change after your trip to Strmica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would those civilian protection -- would that civilian protection team would that [sic] leave the body unburied in Knin when they went with you in the field again, or would they have buried the body first, whether or not in your presence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: They would bury them, regardless of whether I was present on the spot or not. But whether they left them there or not, I'm not certain, but I think they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By -- when you say "left them there," you are referring to left them there not yet being buried? Or how do I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no. As far as I remember, there was one man with the excavator who would dig out a grave and then they would bury them in the graves and they would put crosses there. So it was like that for half a day or a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain the last part of your answer where you said: "So it was like that for half a day or a day."

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was like that for half a day or a day. I said that immediately they would dig a grave with an excavator and they would place bags with dead bodies in the ground. They would put crosses. And they would be received an ID number or first and last name, if the identity was known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now let me take you back to -- later going to Grubori. I think you stated that you told Sacic that you wouldn't want to be filmed or -- when you are doing your job.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. I remember that quite well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us who were with you when you did your job? That is, photographing and taking pictures of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Bilobrk and myself were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sacic did not supervise your work?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sacic brought us to the vicinity of the village in his jeep and then we went to do out work. We photographed and took pictures. Where he was during that time, I really don't know. But I remember that when my colleague Mr. Jozo and I returned, I remember that he was waiting for us next to his jeep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Do you remember at approximately what time you finished your work?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you then go back to Knin again?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you go to the cemetery or did you go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: To the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember, then, what happened at the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were the corpses buried in your presence or not in your presence? Do you know whether they were buried?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember whether they were buried in my presence because I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time does it usually take to do all the paperwork which is related to the sanitation of a body?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: It depends whether the body was fresh or whether putrefaction had begun. It is necessary to take finger-prints on cardboard then to make a list of any scars or if there are personal identification papers on the body, the clothes and the footwear, the place where the body was found, village or hamlet, the time and date, and then two or three photographs are taken, and that's it. I'm not certain how much time is needed, but maybe ten or 15 minutes. It's not easy when you have to take finger-prints on your own, so a colleague usually helps with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection on how difficult and how time-consuming it was to describe and photograph the bodies in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you whether you have any recollection on -- on how difficult and, therefore, how time-consuming, what time it took to describe the bodies and to photograph them, specifically those that you found in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how long it took or whether it was difficult or not. I don't know. There were many of them, so I don't remember it all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no further questions at this moment. Have the questions, cross-examination, or questions by the Bench triggered any further need to re-examination the witness, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There may be just one ambiguity. It may have been cleared up, but I couldn't find it on the screen. But I will see if I can do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You mentioned from the civil protection that there were people in the field and then there was a -- a man or others at the cemetery, a man a with an excavator. Was the civil protection team divided into two?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how they were organised and if they would split into groups or not. But of the four or five of them, five would never go with us, but two or three. And then two would always stay at the cemetery in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That's all I needed to ask. Your Honours, there's a matter arising from cross-examination by the Prosecution. 65 ter 7622. Could that be made an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is the statement to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the joint statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... witness statement. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, the -- yes, the March statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... which is the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- witness 3rd of March --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... 4th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Witness statement of Mr. Vrticevic to my learned friend and his colleagues on the 4th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Until now we have followed procedurally the line that, to the extent certain portions were read or put to the witness, that that would be then on the record, avoiding, thus, to have the whole of the statement, also portions which were not put to a witness, to have that in evidence. But before -- you may remember that we had a similar issue with the Markac Defence. But before we further explore what we did, let's first try to find out whether Mr. Hedaraly in any way objects.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have an objection. It just raises the issue of a statement taken for the purposes of this proceeding. I can guess we can have the witness 92 ter it, I guess, or confirm his signature or something like. But that's my only concern. I have no objection to it being in evidence. It's just I don't know how the Court wishes to deal with it because of the situation that has happened in the past, as the court has pointed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It can't be 92 ter because he said there was a degree of inaccuracy about how parts were written. What I'm concerned with, and it arises from Your Honour's questions because paragraph 7 has a consistency in this witness's evidence which I think this trial will have overlooked or not taken sufficiently into account, if there are any thoughts about the evidence, and in my submission that would be unfair to the accused and the witness. And paragraph 6, paragraph 7, I can go through them with him, if that's required in re-examination, and it arises from Your Honours' questioning. But there are significant features within this statement that go to the consistency of his account in the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you're seeking as a matter of fact is a partial attestation, paragraphs --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you think that should be in evidence; whereas in other respects, especially paragraph 3, you consider not fit to be 92 ter'd, to say it in that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, I have problems with "generally accurate," as to what that means, and I was waiting to see if my learned friend was going to investigate what "generally accurate" means because that carries with it that there may be ungenerally inaccurate parts which don't reflect the whole but do reflect part. And, to be frank, I am not sure how much the proceedings would be served by going into that. I'm quite willing to do so, but I've taken a -- a view on it. I don't know whether that finds favour with the Court or not, and I don't want to burden us with too many aspects of evidence. But paragraphs 6 and 7 are, in my submission, relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest the following. That -- but I'm seeking the parties' advice on the matter. The portion considered relevant by Mr. Hedaraly was almost literally put to the witness, especially what interview the witness was talking about in paragraph 3, who had taken that interview, and -- that is, the Badzim interview, and what he stated in relation to that. I suggest that we slowly read to him paragraphs 6 and 7 to see whether he confirms what he said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we don't have to enter into all kind of technical problems in view of Rule 92 ter. And then it is leading, to some extent, which, of course, is not usually done in examination-in-chief, but here I see Mr. Hedaraly has no problem with it. Mr. Kay, I suggest that you slowly read paragraphs 6 and 7, of which the content you consider to be important, to be part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I'm much obliged to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, I'm going to read a section from your interview by the Prosecution, and if you comment as to whether it's right or wrong, after I've read it. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It comes from paragraph 6 of 65 ter 7622, and it says this: "On the day the human sanitation was carried out in Grubori, I don't remember anything unusual happening in Knin. I don't remember meeting any group of soldiers or any arguments taking place in Knin. It was just business as usual, if I can say." To the best of your knowledge and recollection, what do you say about that statement here?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: That's the truth, what's written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 7: "When we arrived in Plavno, there was quite a number of people there already, including General Cermak, some soldiers in uniform around him who looked like body-guards, and some journalists. I remember that someone wanted to send journalists with us to film us while we carried out our work and ... didn't want my family to see me do this horrible work. I refused and so did Bilobrk. I don't remember how the issue was resolved." What is your comment on -- on that statement, please?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: This is also the truth, as it is recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's all I deal with from the matters arising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, it may be that reviewing some of the evidence and documentation which we'll do over -- during the break, that that may cause the Chamber to add one or more questions. I'm not saying it will, but we, at least, would like to consider that. Under those circumstances, the Chamber would rather take the break now and see, after the break, whether the witness can be excused or not. Is your next witness ready to be called?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. We instructed that that witness be brought here at the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Vrticevic, we'll first take a break. It -- there may be more questions for you but not necessarily. We'll also decide after the break whether you are excused, whether you are free to go or not. But if we would like you to remain stand by, it would be for a limited period of time. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: During the break - I don't know whether you will see anyone else you may know - but you're hereby instructed not to speak with anyone about the questions that were asked, the answers you've given. You should not speak with anyone about it. We'll take a break, and we resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, I have a few questions for, and it concerns a detail of your work in Grubori. Further Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who showed you where the bodies were when you arrived in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But someone must have shown the bodies to you. Or did you have any information as to where to find them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you told us that when you did the job, that is, photographing, et cetera, describing the body, that you were there - if I understand you well - with the civil protection sanitation team, and you and Mr. Bilobrk. Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: In the village, when we were processing the bodies, it was only Robert and me. There were no colleagues from the civil protection there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how did they -- did they wait somewhere? How -- how did this happen?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they were down there together with other people with that group. And when we finished our job related to the bodies, then they went to get the van, to put in the bodies, and then we all left for Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you photograph and describe the bodies all in sequence, and was it after that that the civil protection sanitation team then put all the bodies in the bag? Or did you go from one body to another body; whereas, when had you finished with the first one, that they already put the bodies in the bag?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, when we did our job, whether I did the photographing or Mr. Bilobrk, I don't really remember. Maybe I had the camera. And I also don't remember who was writing the data into the logs. You could probably check it; you could see the signature. But what I do remember is that when we finished all that, the people from the civil protection came. That was the usual procedure. First we did all of our job and then our colleagues came who would then bag the bodies and take them away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you had dealt with all of the bodies and then the civilian protection sanitation team came in, to bag them and to --

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I could remember, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as identification is concerned, do you remember, were the persons who identified the bodies with you, or did they join when the civil protection sanitation team arrived; and where, if they were with you, where did you find them?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do you remember whether they came to where the bodies were, or were they taken to the van in which the bodies were transported?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also -- do you remember whether, at all, any civilians inspected the bodies when you were present?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, on the forms that were produced for each body you found - I think these are called the K-10 forms - now, there is an empty space where photographs can be attached to that form. Is that what usually happened, that the photographs were attached - stapled, glued, I do not know - but, were, usually, the photographs attached to the forms?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat, not to you but to those who took my previous statements, the films and the videos that we made there, we would usually hand over. We would hand them over in the Zadar Police Administration at the crime scene department, Mr. Nevic. Those films were not developed at that time. Whether they developed them later or not and whether they were later attached to those forms, I don't know. Because we also then handed over the forms as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have no further questions for you. Any further questions? Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It may assist on the procedure for identification, if that's a matter Your Honour is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what I wanted to know, as a matter of fact, what the witness can tell about it. But if you want -- I mean, I raised the issue. And if there's any matter you would like to clarify in this respect, please proceed. Further Re-examination by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to the questions His Honour just asked you, would it assist your memory of events if you were able to look at the forms written at the time?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe, yes. But those forms, only if -- if I had filled them, if I had signed them, then everything is as it is in the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Within the KT-10 forms with which you're familiar, there is a written passage on each which says who identified the body to the forensic examiners, the crime technicians. Do you recollect that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA VRTICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is such a place in the form, if somebody can confirm that it is such and such person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kay, I was more interested in whether there they were taken to the bodies or whether the bodies -- whether they had moved. And, of course, I've seen that almost all of them give the same person, identifying the bodies, and -- only one is a bit different. But since the witness has no recollection on how it actually happen, who came to where, who found them, who escort them -- escorted them to the place where the bodies were, therefore, that's the reason why I didn't put any further questions. But it's -- it may be clear that I had that one line in the middle of the KT-10 form on my mind when I asked the witness these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I won't take it any further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any further questions? If not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is about to instruct the witness to remain stand by for the time when the next witness will testify, to see the -- whether there would be any reason to call him back. As I said, the Chamber is about to do that, but if the parties would raise any objections in --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vrticevic, we have concluded your testimony. But the Chamber, nevertheless, would very much like you to remain stand by, most likely for another hour or one hour and a half. So if the evidence to be heard in the next -- in the examination of the next witness would raise any matter which we'd like to hear from you about as well, that you are still there. Therefore, I again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony or to communicate in any other way and to remain at the disposal of the Trial Chamber for -- to start with, the remainder of this morning -- well, let's say, until a quarter to 2.00, unless you will hear otherwise. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom and the next witness could be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Serdarevic. Before you give --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by the usher, and I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Serdarevic. Please be seated. Mr. Serdarevic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Kay. Mr. Kay is counsel for Mr. Cermak. Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Serdarevic, you gave a witness to the Cermak Defence -- a witness statement, and I'd like you to look at the screen in front of you and you will see there an image of the document in your own language will come up onto the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May we have 2D00866 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It's on the right-hand screen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And, I'm sorry, can we have the signature down at the bottom, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Serdarevic, do you recognise that as a witness statement you gave to the Cermak Defence team on the 27th of April, 2010, but signed on the 13th of May, 2010. Do you recognise your signature on the first page of that statement?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the last page of the statement, please, in your language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And do you recognise your signature there on the last page against the date of the 13th of May, 2010?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to read through this statement carefully before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is everything that is contained within that statement, to the best of your knowledge and belief, true and correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I was to ask you in court today the same questions that made up the answers an information in that statement, would your answers today be the same as they were when you made the statement on the 27th of April, 2010?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in those circumstances, might this statement be made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no objections. Madam Registrar, the number for the 92 ter statement of Mr. Serdarevic would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D2053, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D2053 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will give a brief summary of the content of this statement for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Have you not given a similar summary for the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Out of practice, Your Honour, I think, is the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that we should bother this witness with a summary of the statement of the previous witness but perhaps at the end of the day we could -- it could be read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I had that in mind, and Mr. Mak reminded me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Serdarevic made a statement to the Cermak --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you explained to the witness what the purpose of the reading of the summary is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will do, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have not done it yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will do it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Serdarevic, I will give a brief summary of your statement to the Court so that it goes on the record so that anyone listening is aware, in brief terms, what's within your statement. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Serdarevic was a member of the civilian protection team in the MUP in August of 1995, working in the Zadar-Knin area. And in his statement he describes the nature of his work. And his superior was a Mr. Jelic who ran the Knin cemetery. Within the statement, he describes that he was part of the team that collected corpses on the terrain and transported them to the Knin cemetery. There was another team at the cemetery who carried out the burial of the bodies. There was also a further team with which he was not involved that carried out animal sanitation; collecting livestock and carcasses. He describes that there were five members of the team for human sanitation, that they had the use of a van by which they transported corpses in plastic bags. And when they searched the field with crime police officers, the crime police officers took photographs, finger-prints, and wrote a description of the deceased. And they worked on a daily basis with the crime police officers and also pyrotechnicians who also accompanied the teams in their field-work at this time. He described the routine in relation to Knin. Someone would report to the police station, they would be given details of where dead bodies had been located, and they would go and collect with the crime police officers. And it was the crime police officers who received that information first. He describes working with Mr. Bilobrk, as well as Mr. Vrticevic. Location for the bodies came from a variety of people, not only the police but also civilians, Croatian army members, Red Cross, and civilian protection teams dealing with livestock, as well as international representatives. He would remove the mortal remains and bury them with an identification number. And he put the identification number on the corpses and then put the body into the bags which was then put into the van. He describes that the sanitation of the terrain was the exclusive responsibility of the MUP civilian protection employees and not the responsibility of the Croatian army. On the 27th of August, 1995, in that morning, he went to Knin, first of all, and -- having departed from Zadar, and came to Knin between 9.00 and 9.30 in the morning. Mr. Bilobrk was the person who used to go to the police station for information and reports and tell him and his colleagues at a coffee bar where the location was and where they were to go on any day. On the 27th of August, he went to the village of Strmica first, where a single corpse was collected, which was in a decomposed state. From the village of Strmica, he returned to Knin cemetery where the corpse was left and then went to the village of Plavno. He had previously been to the village of Plavno two or three times before; and on the particular day concerned, he was driving the van with four employees of the civilian protection with him. That was the first day that he saw Mr. Cermak, and he saw him in the village of Plavno. When he arrived at a bridge in the village of Plavno, there was a group of people with parked cars. They met on the bridge where people were stopped. And from the village of Plavno, they went to the hamlet of Grubori to collect corpses that needed to be collected there. Mr. Vrticevic was driving the vehicle in front and led the way to Grubori. He couldn't get access to the hamlet with his van, and he describes entering the hamlet of Grubori where he saw some destroyed houses and he found five corpses. And he gives details of what he saw on that day. The crime police officers who were present were the first ones who approached each corpse and did their job. He thinks they carried out an on-site investigation, but he wasn't sure. After they had done their job, he and his colleagues began their work. And they went from one corpse to another and put the identification numbers on the corpses and then placed the bags containing the corpse into the van. And then, from there, the corpses were taken back to Knin. Your Honour, that's a brief summary of the evidence of the witness, Mr. Serdarevic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Serdarevic, just a -- a few general questions arising from your statement. As a member of the MUP civilian protection, did you wear a -- a uniform?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was grey in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that a -- a different coloured uniform from the uniform of police officers?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whilst you were engaged on the 27th of August, 1995, on this task involving the bodies in Grubori, did you hear of anyone making a suggestion that weapons should be planted next to the bodies of the deceased to falsify a crime scene?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On this particular day, you describe going from Knin to Strmica. How long does the journey take from Knin to Strmica?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Some 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your statement records that a body was collected in Strmica on the 27th of August. Can you recollect the state of that corpse on that day at Strmica?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: It was in a state of quite advanced decomposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did it take to deal with the corpse that was part of your tasks at Strmica? How long were you in Strmica for?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't recall that. It wasn't long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And did Mr. Vrticevic and Mr. Bilobrk also go to Strmica on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having been to Strmica and collecting the corpse there, what did you do with that corpse after your visit to Strmica?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: We took it to the town cemetery in Knin where we buried it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it you that did that burial?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Not I. The team working at the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you stay with them while they buried it, or did you unload it from -- from the van and hand it over to them to carry out their task?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: We merely turned the body over to them and proceeded on our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect the length of the journey time from Knin cemetery to Plavno village?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how long it usually took you to go that -- that distance?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: I never measured the kilometres involved. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And then from the cross-roads in -- or from the bridge in Plavno, how far is it up to the hamlet of Grubori? What sort of distance, or how long would it take?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know exactly, but it's not that far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In Grubori hamlet, did you work with the criminal investigation officers, or did they do their tasks separately from you?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: They did their tasks and told us that we could collect the corpses one by one and take them to the town cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have any part to play in the identification of the corpses?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We -- we know from records that the corpses were identified by somebody, and we know your -- from your statement you have a -- a number. Do you know -- did you have any part to play with any of the local people concerning identification by name of the deceased?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And what -- what did that woman do?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: She gave us the names of the people. Only that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's all the questions that I need ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay. Any questions by any other of the Defence teams? If not, Mr. Hedaraly. Are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Serdarevic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Hedaraly is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Serdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you based on the statement that you gave and which is now admitted into evidence as D2053. Now, my -- and it's already on the screen. If we can go to paragraph 12 of your statement first. And before I ask you about this portion of your statement, your superior was Engineer Jelic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And do you know who Engineer Jelic was reporting to?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 12 that do you not know who Mr. Brkic was. Does that mean you never dealt directly with Mr. Brkic? Would that be a fair assumption?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I never communicated with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you don't know whether Mr. Brkic communicated with Mr. Jelic or issued any orders to him or anything of that sort; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you further state in paragraph 12 that as far as you knew -- and I quote: "The Croatian army did not carry out the sanitation of the terrain. The sanitation, human, and animal were exclusively the responsibility of the MUP civilian protection, and we, the civilian protection employees, carried it out. The sanitation was not the responsibility of the Croatian army, nor anyone else."

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was not. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were you aware that there were mixed sanitation teams, including members of the HV, that were involved in human sanitation?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you know that there were orders issued by HV commanders regarding these mixed teams -- mixed sanitation teams?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me move on, then, to paragraph 15 of your statement where you said that you can't give an exact number but you have buried around 200 bodies in the Knin cemetery. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, in your statement, you said that: "I think there were more than 200." Is that a -- is that a fair approximation?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, before burying any of these 200 corpses, was there any examination or autopsies conducted on these bodies?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There were autopsies conducted on these bodies before they were buried?

utterances.speaker: MILE SERDAREVIC
